maria: Quick question — for tenant-local region affinity cutovers, what's our preferred tradeoff between reserved regional capacity vs cross-region failover? Thinking about cost + data residency constraints. cc @jon @lee
jon: I'd avoid maintaining cold GPUs in every region — cost is huge. Prefer thin proxy + cross-region failover for the small % of traffic that needs failover. :thinking_face:
lee: The catch is residency. Some tenants mandate writes stay in the EU. Cross-region failover would violate that unless we implement escrow/consent. Also expect a latency spike for live traffic.
sanjay: Roughly two patterns: (A) resident-only primaries with reserved capacity in each legal region (fast, predictable) (B) primary in one region + geo-redirect on failover with documented consent (cheaper, but legal ops). We need a per-tenant policy flag. Example policy JSON we could use at the routing layer:
```json
{"residency":"eu-only","fallback":"proxy-redirect","fallback-consent":false}
```
maria: That policy example helps. How do we make routing decisions without extra RTTs to the control plane for every request?
anya: Edge idea: store the residency policy in a TTL'd local cache on the edge proxies. On cache miss, proxy asks routing-policy-service. On mismatch we can return 409 + consent header to clients, or for server-server flows do a token exchange. Adds complexity but avoids a synchronous global lookup for each request.
jon: Another lever is prefix/KV cache warming and aggressive prefix hit policies so the failover doesn't need a cold model start. Example dev tool command to prewarm: `prewarm --tenant X --region eu-west-1 --target-gpu 1`
infra-bot: Deploy started: canary routing-policy-service v2 -> eu-west-1 at 2025-09-04T10:12Z
lee: Metrics we should track during experiments: 95p first-token latency, cross-region egress bytes, %requests redirected, and number of residency consent prompts. Also need an audit trail for legal.
sanjay: Quick cost sketch (ballpark): reserving 1 A100 equiv GPU per region ~ $Xk/month vs cross-region egress + occasional burst GPUs ~ $Yk/month for N tenants. I'll flesh this out with actual pricing and include egress per 10k redirected requests.
maria: Nice. Action items: Jon to prototype proxy TTL-caching + prewarm integration, Anya to draft consent UX + API surface, Lee to author residency policy schema + enforcement checklist, Sanjay to run cost model with real numbers. Sync in 48h.
jon: Ack — I'll open a short RFC and attach sample code snippets.
anya: I'll post UX mock and the consent flow diagram in #design later today :+1:
